name: Solanum lycopersicum
description: The garden tomato. Its flowers release pollen best when buzzed, which blue-banded bees do. Gently shaking the trusses helps fruit set when bees are scarce.
fertiliser_note: Too much nitrogen gives leaves instead of fruit. A tomato food with extra potassium helps fruiting.

compost.note: Please bin plants that died of bacterial or fusarium wilt rather than composting them.

care_note: Fruit fly damages ripening fruit in much of Queensland and New South Wales. Netting or fruit bags help.

name: Capsicum annuum
description: Sweet capsicums and most chillies. They need warm weather and set more fruit when bees visit.

name: Solanum melongena
description: A warm-season vegetable with purple, buzz-pollinated flowers that blue-banded bees love.

name: Cucurbita pepo
description: Zucchini and summer squash: bushy plants with large yellow flowers that need bees to set fruit.
care_note: Powdery mildew is common in late summer. Watering the soil rather than the leaves helps.

name: Cucurbita maxima
description: Large pumpkins such as Queensland Blue. The vines sprawl several metres and need bees to set fruit.

name: Cucumis sativus
description: A climbing or sprawling vegetable with yellow flowers in summer.
care_note: Growing it up a trellis keeps the fruit clean and reduces mildew.

name: Phaseolus vulgaris
description: Climbing and dwarf beans. They make their own nitrogen and mostly pollinate themselves.

toxic.note: Raw dried beans contain lectins, so please cook them thoroughly.

name: Pisum sativum
description: Garden peas and snow peas, grown through the cooler months.

name: Lactuca sativa
description: Leafy lettuce, grown quickly in cool weather. In heat it bolts to seed and turns bitter.

name: Brassica oleracea
description: One species with many forms: cabbage, broccoli, cauliflower, kale and brussels sprouts, grown through the cooler months.

name: Beta vulgaris
description: Silverbeet, chard and beetroot. Silverbeet keeps producing leaves for many months.

name: Daucus carota
description: The garden carrot. Plants left to flower make flat white flower heads that feed hoverflies and tiny wasps that eat pests.
fertiliser_note: Fresh manure or too much nitrogen makes roots fork. Please use well-rotted compost dug in beforehand.

name: Allium cepa
description: The bulb onion, sown in autumn and winter in most of Australia.

name: Allium sativum
description: Garlic, planted as cloves in autumn and harvested in late spring or summer.

name: Allium schoenoprasum
description: A clumping herb with mild onion-flavoured leaves and round mauve flowers that bees visit.

name: Zea mays
description: Sweet corn, a tall summer grass. Its pollen is carried by the wind, and honey bees collect it.
care_note: Please plant it in a block of several short rows rather than one long row, so the wind can pollinate the cobs.

name: Ipomoea batatas
description: A sprawling vine grown for its tubers. The young leaves are also edible cooked.
care_note: It spreads vigorously. Please keep the runners out of bushland.

name: Fragaria × ananassa
description: The garden strawberry. Bees improve fruit shape by pollinating every part of the flower.

name: Ocimum basilicum
description: The summer culinary herb. Plants left to flower feed bees well.
pruning: Pinch out flower buds to keep leaves coming, or leave a few plants to flower for bees.

name: Petroselinum crispum
description: Curly and flat-leaf parsley. Plants left to flower in their second year attract hoverflies and small wasps.

name: Coriandrum sativum
description: A fast herb for the cooler months that bolts to seed in heat. Its flowers feed beneficial insects.

name: Foeniculum vulgare
description: A tall aniseed-scented herb with feathery leaves and yellow flower umbels that feed beneficial insects.
care_note: Fennel self-seeds aggressively and is a weed of roadsides and creeks. Please harvest it before it sets seed.

name: Mentha spicata
description: The common garden mint, with small lilac flower spikes in summer that bees and small wasps visit.

name: Thymus vulgaris
description: A low culinary herb with tiny leaves and pale flowers in spring that honey bees love.

name: Origanum vulgare
description: A spreading culinary herb whose small flowers in summer attract bees and butterflies.

name: Cymbopogon citratus
description: A clumping tropical grass with lemon-scented leaves and stems, used in cooking.

name: Citrus × limon
description: The lemon tree, flowering and fruiting on and off for much of the year. Meyer and Eureka are popular backyard varieties.

name: Citrus × sinensis
description: The sweet orange, including navel and Valencia varieties.

name: Citrus reticulata
description: The mandarin, a smaller citrus tree with easy-peel fruit in autumn and winter.

name: Citrus × latifolia
description: The Tahitian lime, a seedless lime that suits warm gardens.

name: Mangifera indica
description: The mango tree. Flies and bees pollinate its sprays of small flowers in late winter. Dwarf varieties suit backyards.

toxic.note: The sap and the skin of the fruit can cause a rash in sensitive people.

care_note: Anthracnose spoils flowers and fruit in wet springs.

name: Persea americana
description: The avocado tree, which needs perfect drainage.

toxic.note: The leaves, skin and stone contain persin, which is poisonous to pet birds and can upset dogs and cats.

care_note: Phytophthora root rot kills avocados in wet soil. Please plant on a mound in a well-drained spot.

name: Carica papaya
description: A fast-growing, short-lived tropical plant with a single trunk and large leaves.
care_note: Plants are male, female or bisexual, so you may need more than one to get fruit.

name: Musa acuminata
description: The banana plant, a giant herb that fruits once from each stem.
care_note: In Queensland, banana plants are regulated to protect commercial crops from disease. Please check Biosecurity Queensland's rules before planting or moving them.

name: Passiflora edulis
description: A vigorous climber with intricate purple-and-white flowers. Large carpenter bees and honey bees pollinate them.
care_note: Most plants are grafted. Please remove suckers from the rootstock, which can take over.

name: Ficus carica
description: The edible fig, a deciduous small tree. Most garden varieties set fruit without pollination.
care_note: Fruit fly and birds target ripe figs. Netting the tree helps.

name: Vaccinium corymbosum
description: The highbush blueberry. Its bell flowers are buzz-pollinated, and low-chill varieties suit subtropical gardens.
fertiliser_note: Please use an azalea and camellia food, which keeps the soil acidic.

name: Olea europaea
description: The olive tree, a long-lived, drought-hardy tree with wind-pollinated flowers.
care_note: Birds spread the fruit, and olives are an environmental weed in parts of South Australia, Victoria and Western Australia.

name: Psidium guajava
description: A small tropical fruit tree with white flowers full of stamens that bees visit.
care_note: Birds spread the seeds, and guava is a weed in parts of tropical Queensland.
